changed.title: Exact shared-line resolution length after replacing binary clauses by private implication chains
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ) (src dst : Fin m → Fin n × Bool) (len : Fin m → ℕ),
  (∀ e, 0 < len e ∧ (src e).1 ≠ (dst e).1) →
  let V := Fin n ⊕ (Fin m × ℕ)
  let lit := fun (e : Fin m) (j : ℕ) =>
    if j = 0 then ((Sum.inl (src e).1 : V), (src e).2)
    else if j = len e then ((Sum.inl (dst e).1 : V), (dst e).2)
    else ((Sum.inr (e,j) : V), true)
  let step := fun (e : Fin m) (j : ℕ) =>
    ({((lit e j).1, !(lit e j).2), lit e (j+1)} : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V)
  let big : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V) := {C | ∃ e j, j < len e ∧ C = step e j}
  let base := fun clauseIndex : Fin m =>
    ({((Sum.inl (src clauseIndex).1 : V), !(src clauseIndex).2), ((Sum.inl (dst clauseIndex).1 : V), (dst clauseIndex).2)} :
      PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V)
  Function.Injective base →
  ∀ K : ℕ,
    (∃ π, PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsRefutation big π ∧ π.length ≤ K) ↔
    ∃ S : Finset (Fin m), ∃ π, PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsRefutation
      {C | ∃ idx ∈ S, C = base idx} π ∧ π.length + 2*S.sum (fun idx => len idx-1) ≤ K
changed.unlocks: prices shared resolution lines after each binary clause is replaced with its own private implication path
changed.context: Expand each used original axiom once and share its chain. In reverse choose a breakpoint missing from each incomplete chain and any breakpoint for each complete one. Substitute endpoint literals on either side. All links except breakpoints become tautologies. A connected component of discarded tautological lines with a axiom nodes needs at least a−1 internal inferences and loses a distinct boundary inference. This removes at least two lines per discarded tautological input and leaves a proof from complete chains.

changed.title: Exact tree-like resolution leaf cost after replacing binary clauses by private implication chains
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ) (src dst : Fin m → Fin n × Bool) (len : Fin m → ℕ),
  (∀ e, 0 < len e ∧ (src e).1 ≠ (dst e).1) →
  let V := Fin n ⊕ (Fin m × ℕ)
  let lit := fun (e : Fin m) (j : ℕ) =>
    if j = 0 then ((Sum.inl (src e).1 : V), (src e).2)
    else if j = len e then ((Sum.inl (dst e).1 : V), (dst e).2)
    else ((Sum.inr (e,j) : V), true)
  let step := fun (e : Fin m) (j : ℕ) =>
    ({((lit e j).1, !(lit e j).2), lit e (j+1)} : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V)
  let big : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V) := {C | ∃ e j, j < len e ∧ C = step e j}
  let base := fun clauseIndex : Fin m =>
    ({((Sum.inl (src clauseIndex).1 : V), !(src clauseIndex).2), ((Sum.inl (dst clauseIndex).1 : V), (dst clauseIndex).2)} :
      PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V)
  Function.Injective base →
  let tree := fun (leaf : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V → ℕ → Prop) (K : ℕ) =>
    ∃ (nodes inner : Finset (List Bool)) (line : List Bool → PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V)
      (cost : List Bool → ℕ), [] ∈ nodes ∧ inner ⊆ nodes ∧ line [] = ∅ ∧
      (nodes \ inner).sum cost ≤ K ∧
      (∀ p ∈ nodes, p ∉ inner → leaf (line p) (cost p)) ∧
      (∀ (p : List Bool) (a : Bool), p ++ [a] ∈ nodes → p ∈ inner) ∧
      ∀ p ∈ inner, p ++ [false] ∈ nodes ∧ p ++ [true] ∈ nodes ∧
        PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsResolvent (line (p ++ [false])) (line (p ++ [true])) (line p)
  ∀ K : ℕ,
    tree (fun C charge => C ∈ big ∧ charge = 1) K ↔
    tree (fun D price => ∃ idx, D = base idx ∧ price = len idx) K
changed.unlocks: computes the independent tree leaf cost under private path substitution using weighted original leaf occurrences
changed.context: At each original leaf resolve the chain to recover that clause with t_e leaves. In reverse pick one uniformly random breakpoint in each chain. Map the private literals on the two sides to the two endpoint literals. All links except the breakpoint become tautologies. Project the resolution tree by pruning tautologies and keeping subclauses. Each leaf on chain e survives as a candidate with probability 1/t_e and carries weight t_e, so some projected tree has weight at most the original leaf count.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt. Guarded width bounds give a b-way Promise-Ball-SAT search within radius r
changed.statement:
∀ (n b r : Nat), 0 < b →
  let V := Fin n
  let Point := V → Bool
  let Clause := Finset (V × Bool)
  let sat := fun (formula : Finset Clause) (x : Point) =>
    ∀ c ∈ formula, ∃ lit ∈ c, x lit.1 = lit.2
  ∀ (clauses : List Clause) (center : Point),
    let F := clauses.toFinset
    let bad := fun (x : Point) (c : Clause) => ∀ lit ∈ c, x lit.1 ≠ lit.2
    let vars := fun (c : Clause) => c.image Prod.fst
    let state := fun (flipped : Finset V) (v : V) =>
      if v ∈ flipped then !(center v) else center v
    let run := fun (choices : Fin r → Fin b) =>
      (List.finRange r).foldl (fun used step =>
        let c := (clauses.find? (fun d => decide (bad (state used) d))).getD ∅
        let options := ((vars c) \ used).sort (· ≤ ·)
        let picked := options[ (choices step).val ]?
        used ∪ picked.toList.toFinset) (∅ : Finset V)
    (∀ c ∈ F, (vars c).card ≤ b+1) →
    (∀ c ∈ F, bad center c → (vars c).card ≤ b) →
    ((∃ y : Point, sat F y ∧ ((Finset.univ : Finset V).filter (fun i => y i ≠ center i)).card ≤ r) ↔
      (∃ choices : Fin r → Fin b, sat F (state (run choices))))
changed.unlocks: Rebuilds the bounded Promise-Ball-SAT branching step with both width promises guarding the equivalence.
changed.context: Maintain agreement of flipped bits with a chosen nearby model. A false clause has an unflipped variable on which the current word differs from that model. If it was false initially it has at most b variables. If it was true initially, at least one of its at most b+1 variables is already flipped. Hence a valid branch selects the useful variable and reduces distance by one. Once satisfied, all remaining steps are idle. Conversely the procedure flips at most r bits.
